sections.h2: What sets Morgan County apart in north central Georgia?
sections.html:
Morgan County pairs a historic seat in Madison with a share of the lake country, and its housing boom since the early 2000s comes from easy reach of Lake Oconee and four employment centers: Atlanta, Athens, Augusta and Macon. Lawmakers carved the county out on December 10, 1807, as Wikipedia recounts.

The county spans 355 square miles, with 7.3 of them water, and every part of it drains to the Upper Oconee River. Interstate 20 runs through, joined by U.S. 129 and U.S. 441 (with a bypass around Madison), U.S. 278, and state routes 83 and 186. The county takes in part of the Oconee National Forest. Oconee, Greene, Putnam, Jasper, Newton and Walton counties are the neighbors.

Madison, Bostwick and Rutledge are cities, Buckhead is a town, and Godfrey is a census-designated place. Apalachee and Pennington are unincorporated communities. Madison levies its own city tax on top of the county's, so an owner inside the city limits has two sets of charges to keep in view when selling.

sections.h2: How have Morgan County home values and population changed?
sections.html:
Morgan County homes are priced high for the region: the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $342,300 for 2020 to 2024, and population up 10.0% from the April 2020 base to July 2025, according to Census QuickFacts.

The head count rose from 17,868 in 2010 to 20,097 in 2020. Among adults 25 and older, 29.7% hold a bachelor's degree; 22.3% of all residents are 65 or older; and 10.6% live in poverty. Travel to work averages 28.5 minutes. Shoppers spent $23,226 per resident in 2022, and hotels and restaurants took in $72,574,000.

sections.h2: Which two Morgan County offices split the tax work?
sections.html:
Collecting and valuing sit in separate county offices, the Tax Commissioner and the Tax Assessor. The commissioner's county page lists collection of property, mobile home and timber taxes, tag sales and renewals, and title transfers. Anyone doing business there needs a Georgia driver's license or ID showing a Morgan County address.

The Tax Assessor's office takes returns and homestead applications at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, Madison, GA 30650. The filing window for returns runs January 2 to April 1. Challenges start at that desk and can go on to the grand jury's appointees on the Board of Equalization. The county's Board of Commissioners sets the county budget and the county mill rate, and the Board of Education recommends a school rate that, with very few exceptions, the commissioners must levy.

The state limits its own levy to one fourth of a mill. Ask the commissioner's office whether the Madison city bill arrives separately from the county bill.

sections.h2: What property tax deadline does Morgan County print?
sections.html:
On its tax commissioner page, Morgan County calls November 15 the official deadline and says penalties and interest accrue after it. State guidance names December 20 as the default and lets a county move to December 1 or November 15, which is the route Morgan took.

The same page says you may pay online through the county's online tax payment system. State officials add that taxpayers get 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts, so look at the bill itself before assuming a day. The office also collects mobile home and timber tax, so ask the counter for those dates.

A buyer who closes after January 1 should confirm who carries that year's bill, because under state guidance the January 1 owner is the one liable.

sections.h2: Which homestead and senior exemptions does Morgan County list?
sections.html:
Morgan County's assessor page lists a ladder of exemptions that stack on the state basics. The county page spells out each one, and the assessors decide eligibility.

  • Standard homestead: as much as $2,000 comes off the assessed value, which is 40% of market value, for county, school and state operating levies.
  • Age 65 and up: a further $10,000 comes off the county and school operating portion, with no income test.
  • Madison residents over 65: another $10,000 off for city maintenance and operations tax.
  • Standard elderly: up to $4,000 off for owners 65 and older whose net income with a spouse stays at or below $10,000, with Social Security and some retirement income excluded.
  • Age 65 and older, state levy: an exemption equal to the full value of the home and up to 10 acres.
  • Disabled veterans rated 100% service connected: a larger deduction that changes every year, with a DD214 and Veterans Affairs letter required.
  • Surviving spouses: up to $50,000 for an unremarried spouse of a service member who died in war or armed conflict, and a full exemption for the unremarried spouse of a firefighter or peace officer who died in the line of duty.

sections.h2: How do I file or keep a Morgan County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Take the application to the Tax Assessor. Walk it in during any month. April 1 is the cutoff for the current year, and the house must be your residence on January 1.

Once approved, the exemption rolls forward by itself. A new filing is needed only after a change of ownership, a move, a switch to a different kind of exemption, or when the exemption depends on income. If the Board of Assessors denies an application, the county must tell the applicant, and an appeal path is available. The page also points to conservation use and personal property information under the assessor menu for farmland owners and business owners.

sections.h2: How does a Morgan County value appeal work?
sections.html:
When the Board of Tax Assessors mails a notice of a changed value, the owner has 45 days to respond. The board looks again and sends back its decision. A taxpayer still unhappy moves up to the Board of Equalization for a hearing, or picks arbitration instead when first filing.

The county page limits the grounds to taxability, value and uniformity compared with similar properties. Grumbling about the size of the bill does not qualify, and late filings are barred. Superior court remains open after the administrative step. A new return filed during the January 2 to April 1 window can set a different value and protect your appeal rights if the board raises it again.

sections.h2: What else in Morgan County government affects a house sale?
sections.html:
Morgan County lists a Planning and Development department with zoning information, flood plain management information, a fee schedule and a comprehensive plan, plus a Roads and Bridges department that publishes a mowing schedule and a road resurfacing list. Check the zoning page and the flood plain page if the lot is near water.

Court Services covers Magistrate Court, Probate Court and Superior Court, which matters for an inherited house. The county's Solid Waste and Sanitation page includes recycling. QuickFacts counts 573 employer businesses with 6,763 jobs in 2023, and 87.1% of households have a broadband subscription. It also counts 963 veterans, of whom only those rated 100% service connected qualify for the disabled veteran exemption listed above.

sections.h2: What should a Morgan County seller settle on tax before closing?
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the tax commissioner, and ask your closing attorney who covers the November 15 bill if the sale closes first. The Department of Revenue says no refund exists for part of a year, so proration lives in the contract.

A Madison address adds a city bill, so ask which office collects it. Sellers over 65 should check that the exemptions above are on the account before the buyer's lender reviews the tax figures. A buyer who will live in the home must file a separate homestead application by the next April 1.

faqs.q: What is Morgan County's official property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 15, according to the commissioner's page, after which penalties and interest build.

faqs.q: Who takes Morgan County homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor, at 150 E Washington Street, Suite 130, in Madison. Aim for April 1 if you want the savings this year.

faqs.q: Can I pay Morgan County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online tax payment system that the commissioner's page links to.

faqs.q: Does Morgan County give seniors an extra exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Residents 65 and older can take an additional $10,000 off assessed value for county and school maintenance and operations, with no income limit, and Madison residents can add the same amount for city tax.

faqs.q: What is the window for a Morgan County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting with the notice of changed value, and the first stop is the Board of Tax Assessors.
